title: Coral and the Parish
premise: Ivo Yarrow, archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, discovers a drowned body in the locked crypt wearing clothes taken from her own wardrobe — and the dead woman is wearing Ivo's missing sister's locket. The case everyone believes closed, the drowning of verger's daughter Coral Fen nine years ago, turns out to have been buried deliberately, with the crypt locked to hide a second grave. As Ivo digs through parish records and her own fractured memory, she realizes the killer is someone rewriting the parish's history to protect a legacy of abuse, and that the body in her clothes was a message meant to make her stop. In the end Ivo exposes the dean who orchestrated both deaths, reopens the crypt as a memorial, and finally admits the truth about her sister's disappearance — that Coral was her sister, and she has been erasing her own memory to survive.
about_author: Mirabel Amberdale is a former parish secretary from the West Country who spent a decade cataloguing church records before turning to fiction. She writes quiet, claustrophobic mysteries about small communities and the documents they would rather lose.

chapters.title: The Locked Door Below
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. During a routine inventory of the cathedral crypt, Ivo finds the inner door unlocked for the first time in nine years — and a drowned body inside, dressed in clothes from her own closet. The chapter establishes her meticulous, guarded character and ends with her recognizing the locket on the dead woman's neck. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professional calm.

chapters.title: Clothes That Fit a Stranger
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Police question Ivo, who cannot explain the missing garments or why she never reported the closet theft. Detective Sergeant Halloway notes the dead woman's fingerprints match no record. Ivo privately compares the locket to one she remembers from childhood and burns a note rather than show it. Emotional beat: the first crack in her composure.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, with a flashback to Coral Fen's funeral, which Ivo did not attend. The parish closed the drowning case quickly; the verger, Edric Fen, still leaves flowers at a locked gate. Ivo interviews Edric, who says his daughter never swam and never went near the crypt. Emotional beat: grief fossilized into routine, and Ivo's guilt sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Blank Page
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. In the archive, Ivo finds the crypt access log torn out — the only missing page in thirty years of immaculate records. She notices the dean, Ambrose Pell, signed the last entry before the gap. Pell is charming, beloved, and now presiding over the cathedral's 500th-anniversary restoration. Emotional beat: suspicion arriving dressed as courtesy.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Halloway's POV. The police identify the victim as Ruth Ellery, a former choirgirl who left the parish abruptly in 2016. Halloway interviews Pell, who smoothly redirects to the cathedral's reputation and hints Ivo may be unstable. Halloway, new to the town, senses a wall of polite obstruction. Emotional beat: an outsider's unease in a place where everyone agrees too easily.

chapters.title: The Sister I Don't Have
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Searching her childhood home, Ivo finds a photo of two girls by the river — herself and a girl her mother insisted was a cousin. Her hands shake as she realizes the locket in the crypt is engraved with a date from her own family. She begins to suspect Coral Fen was never Edric's daughter at all. Emotional beat: memory as a locked room she has been avoiding.

chapters.title: Choir of the Disappeared
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo tracks down three women who sang in the choir with Ruth Ellery and Coral. All three left town within two years of Coral's death. One, now estranged from the church, tells Ivo the choir was Pell's private kingdom and that complaints were 'handled' by the parish council. Emotional beat: the horror of a pattern, not an accident.

chapters.title: A Second Grave
chapters.summary: Halloway's POV. Ground-penetrating radar commissioned quietly for the restoration reveals a second cavity beneath the crypt floor. Halloway wants to excavate; the diocese stalls, citing consecrated ground. Pell offers Halloway a transfer-friendly outcome if the matter is handled 'internally.' Emotional beat: power flexing through paperwork.

chapters.title: Edric's Silence
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo confronts Edric Fen with the photo. He breaks: Coral was placed with him as a foster child after her mother's death, and he suspected what Pell was doing but stayed silent to keep his position — and because Coral begged him not to intervene. He believes Coral's drowning was an accident born of shame. Emotional beat: complicity confessed, forgiveness withheld.

chapters.title: The Message in My Clothes
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Forensics confirm Ruth Ellery died recently, not nine years ago, and that someone with access to Ivo's home dressed the body. Ivo realizes the staging was aimed at her specifically — someone who knows who she is and what she's remembering. She installs a lock on her own bedroom door and stops sleeping. Emotional beat: paranoia closing in like weather.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Fund
chapters.summary: Halloway's POV. Halloway follows the restoration money: a trust administered by Pell has quietly paid settlements to several former choir members, all bound by NDAs. One payout was signed by Ivo's mother. The trail suggests Ivo's family took hush money and left town — which is why Ivo's childhood is a fog. Emotional beat: the discovery that her own memory may have been purchased.

chapters.title: Mother's Confession, Half Spoken
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo visits her mother in a care home. Between lucid moments, her mother says: 'We took the money so you'd forget. Coral wanted to testify. You were the witness, Ivo. You saw.' The chapter ends with Ivo remembering the riverbank — Pell, Coral, and herself, hidden behind the boathouse. Emotional beat: the floodgate breaking.

chapters.title: What I Saw at the Water
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, intercut with a full flashback. Nine years ago, Ivo witnessed Pell follow Coral to the river after she threatened to go public. Coral fell; Pell held her under; Ivo fled and told her mother, who chose the settlement. The 'closed case' was built on Ivo's silence. Emotional beat: shame transmuting into fury.

chapters.title: Ruth Ellery's Letters
chapters.summary: Halloway and Ivo's POV alternating. Ruth Ellery had been writing to Coral's old address for years, collecting testimony from choir survivors for a book. Her last letter names Pell and mentions 'the page from the ledger.' Someone intercepted her letters — the forwarding address belongs to the parish office. Emotional beat: two investigations converging on one man.

chapters.title: The Dean's Sermon
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the 500th-anniversary service, Pell preaches on forgiveness and forgetting, looking directly at Ivo. Afterward he privately warns her: her mother's signature is on documents that could ruin Ivo too, and the crypt will be sealed again Monday. The threat is flawless, deniable, and effective. Emotional beat: terror of a man who wields the parish like a weapon.

chapters.title: Breaking Ground
chapters.summary: Halloway's POV. Halloway defies the diocese and excavates the second grave with Edric Fen's blessing: it is Coral Fen, moved from the river grave years after her funeral — proof of concealment, not accident. The parish fractures; half the congregation defends Pell. Emotional beat: a town's foundation cracking open.

chapters.title: Night in the Archive
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Someone breaks into the archive to burn the reconstructed ledger; Ivo interrupts them and is attacked. She escapes with a scorched page bearing Pell's initials and a payment code matching Ruth's notes. Halloway arrives too late to catch the intruder — a verger's key was used. Emotional beat: Ivo bleeding, but no longer afraid.

chapters.title: The Council of the Complicit
chapters.summary: Halloway's POV. Halloway traces the NDA payments to three parish council members who enabled Pell for decades. One, facing ruin, agrees to testify in exchange for immunity and hands over recordings Pell made 'for the church's protection' — which include the night of Coral's death. Emotional beat: the machinery of silence eating itself.

chapters.title: The Crypt at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Pell lures Ivo to the crypt with a message in Ruth's handwriting, intending to stage her death as a copycat. Ivo, expecting it, wears a wire. In the dark he confesses — Coral, Ruth, the ledger, the clothes stolen to unmake her. Halloway and officers take him as he reaches for the sluice lever. Emotional beat: the witness finally speaking, and being heard.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Halloway's POV. Pell is charged; the diocese collapses the trust; survivors, including the three choirwomen, give statements. Ivo testifies about what she saw at nine years old, her mother's choice, and her own long silence. Edric Fen sits in the gallery holding Coral's photograph. Emotional beat: grief given a public room at last.

chapters.title: Unlocking the Door
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo catalogues the reopened crypt as a memorial, Coral's and Ruth's names cut into the stone. She returns the locket to Edric, tells him the whole truth of who Coral was, and forgives him — and asks, without expecting it, whether he can forgive her silence. He can. Emotional beat: mourning becoming remembrance.

chapters.title: The Archive of the Living
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, epilogue. A year later, Ivo has established an independent archive of survivor testimony, open to all, answerable to no dean. She writes Coral's full story in her own hand and files it under her sister's true name. The last line: memory is not a locked room but a door she now leaves open. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed, quiet and whole.
